items.summary_1line: We ask what AI coding agents and AI security harnesses find that deterministic static application security testing (SAST) does not, and what they miss that SAST catches. VulnBench 2.0 is a benchmark of 108 hand-curate...

items.title: CRESiST: Self-Enhancing Explorative Policy Learning for Simultaneous Speech Translation
items.summary_1line: Simultaneous Speech Translation (SimulST) requires balancing translation quality and latency. While Large Language Models (LLMs) excel in offline translation, current LLM-based SimulST systems predominantly rely on pr...

items.title: PromptOps: Iterative Prompt Optimization for LLM-as-a-Judge Systems
items.summary_1line: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges for evaluating the behavior of chatbots and other AI systems. In deployment, however, their agreement with the intended human evaluation policy may degrade as user interactions and score distributions change.
items.editor_note: Iterative prompt optimization keeps an LLM judge aligned with a human evaluation policy as scores drift.

items.title: Learning Multi-Agent Orchestration:Higher-Order Interactions in Policy Improvement
items.summary_1line: Learned orchestration has emerged as a promising paradigm for large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems, in which a central orchestrator selects agents and controls the information they receive throughout a...
items.editor_note: Models higher-order interactions among agents when learning an orchestrator's policy.

editorial.tldr: ReflectPO (Oct 22) and SOPO (Oct 23) applied policy optimization to long-horizon agents and span-level hallucination detection. By Oct 27-28 papers argued the policy and its harness must be judged together, and Snyk VulnBench 2.0 measured harness policy and cost against deterministic SAST.
editorial.whats_new: A Nov 5 preprint on learned multi-agent orchestration models higher-order interactions in policy improvement, following Nov 4's PromptOps for LLM-as-a-judge drift and tree-branching TSBPO (Oct 30).
editorial.why_it_matters: Optimization targets are widening from the model to the orchestrator, the prompt and the judge, so each moving part of an agent stack needs its own regression eval.
editorial.take_for_builders: Treat these as preprints: wait for code and replication before changing a training pipeline, and rerun agent evals whenever the harness, prompt or judge changes, not only the model.

status.detail: Preprint-only thread: methods span agents, judges and orchestration, with no code or replication reported in these items.

beats.headline: Reflection-guided and multiscale optimization for long-horizon agents and hallucination spans
Policy and harness are treated as one system
Credit assignment and sampling: tree branching for language agents, GRPO for few-step flow models
Policy learning moves to judges, translation and multi-agent orchestration

open_questions: Do any of these methods publish code or reproducible results on public benchmarks?
Does VulnBench 2.0 get run by anyone outside Snyk's authors?
Do harness-aware evaluations change reported rankings of agents versus bare-model scores?
Does learned orchestration beat hand-written orchestration on an independent multi-agent benchmark?
